questions.q: A chain of mass $m$ forming a circle of radius $\text{R}$ is slipped on a smooth round cone with half-angle $\text{\theta}$. Find the tension in the chain if it rotates with a constant angular velocity $\text{\omega}$ about a vertical axis coinciding with the symmetry axis of the cone.
questions.solution:
Every element of chain moves on a circular path. So, every element of the chain experiences centripetal force. We consider a small element $\Delta\text{m}$ on the chain making angle $\text{\Delta \theta}$ at the centre





$\text{\Delta N sin \theta = \Delta mg}$...... (i)

Net force towards centre is

$2 \text{T} \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{N} \text\cos \theta = \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}$

$\Delta N ⁡ \text\cos \theta = 2 T ⁡ \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}$.......... (ii)

From eqn.(i) and (ii) we get

$\text\cos \theta = \dfrac{2 \text{T} \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}}{\Delta \text{mg}}$

But $\text{\Delta \theta}$ is very small.

∴ $\text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} = \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2}$

∵ $\text\cot \theta = \dfrac{\text{T} \Delta \theta - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}}{\Delta \text{mg}}$

Here Δm makes an angle Δθ at the centre. The total mass of chain is m.

∴ The mass of chain per unit angle is

$\lambda = \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi}$

∴ $\Delta m ⁡ = \lambda \Delta \theta = \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi} \Delta \theta = \dfrac{m ⁡ \Delta \theta}{2 \pi}$

∴ $\text\cot\theta = \dfrac{\text{T}\Delta\theta - \left(\dfrac{m\Delta\theta}{2\pi}\right)R{ω}^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{m}{2\pi} \Delta\theta\right)g}$

∴ $T ⁡ = \left(R ⁡ {ω}^{2} + \text{g} \text\cot \theta\right) \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi}$

questions.solution:
Angular momentum of a rigid body about a fixed axis is given by

$L = I\omega$

Where $I$ is moment of inertia and $\omega$ is angular velocity about that axis.

Kinetic energy of body is given by

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$

$∴K = \dfrac{1}{2I}{\left(I\omega\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{L^{2}}{2I}$

$⇒I = \dfrac{L^{2}}{2K}$

questions.solution:
When the rod rotates through angle $\theta$, the fall $h$ of centre of gravity is given by $\theta$

$\dfrac{\dfrac{L}{2} - h}{\dfrac{L}{2}} = cos\left(\theta\right)$

 

or$h = \dfrac{L}{2} ( 1 - cos\theta )$

Decrease in potential energy

$= Mgh = Mg\dfrac{L}{2} ( 1 - cos\theta )$

Now, $KE$ of rotation $= \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{{ML}^{2}}{3}{\omega}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{{ML}^{2}}{3}{\omega}^{2}$

$\left[I = {ML}^{2} / 3\right$ (because rod is rotating about an axis passing through its one end) 

According to law of conservation of energy, decrease in potential energy will be equal to gain in kinetic energy.

$Mg\dfrac{L}{2} ( 1 - cos\theta ) = \dfrac{M{L}^{2}}{6}{\omega}^{2}$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{L} ( 1 - Cos\theta )} = \sqrt{\dfrac{6g}{L}}Sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}$

The distance of the centre of mass from the hinge,

$\omega = \dfrac{v}{2l}$

The moment of inertia of the system about the hinge,

$I = m{l}^{2} + m{\left(2l\right)}^{2} = 5m{l}^{2}$

The rotational kinetic energy of the system,

${K}_{R} = \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}5m{l}^{2}{\left(\dfrac{v}{2l}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {K}_{R} = \dfrac{5m{v}^{2}}{8}$

$\dfrac{{K}_{cm}}{{K}_{R}} = \dfrac{9m{v}^{2}}{16} \times \dfrac{8}{5m{v}^{2}} = 0 . 9$

questions.q: In the diagram shown, a rod of mass $M$ has been fixed on a ring of the same mass. The whole system has been placed on a perfectly rough surface. The system is gently displaced so that the ring starts rolling. The velocity of the centre of the ring when the rod becomes horizontal is (the length of the rod is equal to the radius of the ring)
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of the system about instantaneous axis of rotation is given by,

$I = {I}_{ring} + {I}_{rod}$

$⇒ I = ( {MR}^{2} + {MR}^{2} ) + \left(\dfrac{1}{12}{MR}^{2} + {MR}_{1}^{2}\right) & & & (From parallel axis theorem)

$⇒ I = 2{MR}^{2} + $\dfrac{1}{12}{MR}^{2} +$ M $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}R}{2}\right)2$ & & & & & $\left(∵ {R}_{1} = \sqrt{R^{2} + \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)22}=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}$ R}{2}\right)

$⇒ I = 2{MR}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{12}{MR}^{2} + \dfrac{5}{4}{MR}^{2} = 2{MR}^{2} + \dfrac{4}{3}{MR}^{2} = \dfrac{10}{3}{MR}^{2}$

Hence, ${I}_{system} = \dfrac{10}{3}{MR}^{2}.

Now$ from work - energy theorem, we get,

Mg$\dfrac{R}{2} =Rotational kinetic energy of the system about instantaneous axis of rotation
(here \dfrac{R}{2} is the distance through which the center of mass of the rod descends)

$⇒ Mg$\dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{system}{ω}^{2}$

$⇒ Mg\dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{10}{3}{MR}^{2} \times {ω}^{2}$

$⇒ $\omega = $\sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{10R}$}$

Now velocity of center of mass is given as, $v = R $\omega.
$⇒ v = R \times \sqrt{$\dfrac{3g}{10R}}$
$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{3gR}{10}$}$

$

Slipping will be stopped when $v = r \omega$

& & & & $at = r ( {ω}_{0} - \alpha t )$

$ \text{\mu} \text{gt} = \text{r} ( {ω}_{0} - \dfrac{5}{2} \dfrac{\text{\mu} \text{g} \text{t}}{\text{r}} )$

$ \dfrac{7}{2} \text{\mu} \text{gt} = \text{r} {ω}_{0}$

questions.q: A metre stick is balanced on a knife-edge at its centre. When two coins, each of mass 5 g are put one on top of the other at the 12 cm mark, the stick is found to be balanced at 45.0 cm. What is the mass (in gram) of the metre stick?
questions.solution:
Let total mass of the metre stick be M gram



Distance between mid-point E and new centre of gravity (DE),

= 50 - 45 = 5 cm

Distance between 12 cm mark and new centre of gravity (CD),

= 45 - 12 = 33 cm

From principle of moments in equilibrium,

Mg × DE = (2 × 5g) × CD

M × 5 = 10 × 33
​
or M = 66 g

∴ Mass of the metre stick is 66 g.

questions.q: A lamina is made by removing a small disc of diameter $2R$ from a bigger disc of uniform mass density and radius $2R$, as shown in the figure. If the ratio $\dfrac{{I}_{P}}{{I}_{O}} = \dfrac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are the smallest integers, then what is the value of $m + n$?
questions.solution:
${\text{I}}_{\text{P}} = \left[\dfrac{4 \text{m} {\text{R}}^{2}}{2} + \text{m} \left(4 {\text{R}}^{2}\right)\right] - \left[\dfrac{\text{m}}{4} \dfrac{{\text{R}}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{\text{m}}{4} 5 {\text{R}}^{2}\right]$

${\text{I}}_{\text{P}} = {\text{mR}}^{2} \left[\left(2 + 4\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{5}{4}\right)\right]$

${\text{I}}_{\text{P}} = {\text{mR}}^{2} \left(6 - \dfrac{1 1}{8}\right) = \dfrac{3 7}{8} {\text{mR}}^{2} \ldots \left(1\right)$

${\text{I}}_{O} = \left(\dfrac{4{\text{mR}}^{2}}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{\text{m}}{4}\dfrac{{\text{R}}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{\text{m}}{4}{\text{R}}^{2}\right)$

${\text{I}}_{O} = {\text{mR}}^{2}\left[2 - \left(\dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\right] = {\text{mR}}^{2}\left[2 - \dfrac{3}{8}\right] = {\text{mR}}^{2}\left(\dfrac{13}{8}\right) \ldots \left(2\right)$

$So \dfrac{{\text{I}}_{\text{P}}}{{\text{I}}_{\text{O}}} = \dfrac{37 / 8}{13 / 8} = \dfrac{37}{13}$

$⇒ m + n = 37 + 13 = 50$

$\text{So} \overset{\to}{\text{L}} = \text{m} | \begin{cases}\overset{\to}{\text{i}} & \overset{\to}{\text{j}} & \overset{\to}{\text{k}} \\ \dfrac{{\text{0.7v}}_{0}^{2}}{\text{g}} & \dfrac{{\text{0.2v}}_{0}^{2}}{\text{g}} & 0 \\ {\text{0.7v}}_{0} & - {\text{0.3v}}_{0} & 0\end{cases} |$

$\text{i.e.,} \overset{\to}{\text{L}} = - \left({\text{0.35mv}}_{0}^{3} / \text{g}\right) \overset{\to}{\text{k}}$

i.e., angular momentum has magnitude $\text{0.35} {\text{mv}}_{0}^{3} / \text{g}$ and is directed along negative z-axis.

$⇒ n = \dfrac{\theta}{2\pi} = \dfrac{\left(1 + {\mu}^{2}\right)R{\omega}^{2}}{8\pi\mug\left(\mu + 1\right)}$

questions.q: A rope of negligible mass is wound around a hollow cylinder of mass 3 kg and radius 40 cm and then the entire arrangement is placed on a smooth horizontal surface. What is the angular acceleration (in $rad{s}^{- 2}$) of the cylinder if the rope is pulled with a  force of 30 N?
questions.solution:
Given, M = 3 kg

R = 40 cm = 0.40 m

F = 30 N

Moment of inertia of the hollow cylinder about its axis of symmetry

I = MR2

= 3 × (0.40)2 = 0.48 kg-m2

Torque acting on the cylinder by the applied force,

$τ$ = F × R

= 30 × 0.40 = 12 N-m.

Angular acceleration produced in cylinder,

$\text{\alpha} = \dfrac{\text{τ}}{\text{I}} = \dfrac{\text{12}}{\text{0.48}} = {\text{25 rad/s}}^{2}$

Linear acceleration, a = R$\alpha$

= 0.40 × 25 = 10.0 m/s2

questions.q: A rod of length $l ⁡$ = $2m$ is maintained to rotate with a constant angular velocity $\omega = {\text{1 rad s}}^{- 1}$ about a vertical axis passing through one end (diagram). One end of the spring is attached to the axis of rotation. $S$ is a sleeve of mass $m = 1kg$ which can just fit on rod. All surfaces are smooth. With what minimum kinetic energy (in j) sleeve should be projected so that it enters on the rod without jerk and completely compresses the spring.
questions.solution:
For entering without jerk ${\text{v}}_{2} = l ⁡ {\omega}_{0} = {\text{2 m s}}^{- 1}$

Using work-energy theorem on the sleeve after entering in the frame of rod



${\text{W}}_{\text{spring}} + {\text{W}}_{\text{centrifugal}} = \Delta \text{K}$

$- \dfrac{1}{2} \text{k} {l ⁡}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \text{m} {\omega}^{2} {l ⁡}^{2} = 0 - \dfrac{1}{2} {\text{mv}}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ {\text{v}}_{1}^{2} = 8$

Now, $\text{K} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{m} \left({\text{v}}_{1}^{2} + {\text{v}}_{2}^{2}\right) = 6$

questions.q: A solid sphere and hollow sphere of the same mass and radius are given a spin about their centre of mass and then, they are placed on a rough horizontal surface. The spin angular velocity is the same for both the spheres and it is equal to ${ω}_{0}$. Once the pure rolling starts; let ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ be the linear speeds of their centres of mass, then
questions.solution:
From conservation of angular momentum about point of contact :



$\text{I} {ω}_{0} = \text{I} \omega + \text{mRv}$
or $\text{I} {ω}_{0} = \text{I} \dfrac{\text{v}}{\text{R}} + \text{mRv}$
or $\text{v} = \dfrac{\text{I} {ω}_{0}}{\dfrac{\text{I}}{\text{R}} + \text{mR}}$
or
or $\text{v} = \dfrac{{ω}_{0}}{\dfrac{1}{\text{R}} + \dfrac{\text{mR}}{\text{I}}}$
Now ${I}_{\text{solid} \text{sphere < }} {I}_{hollow}$
∴ ${v}_{\text{solid} < } {v}_{hollow}$
∴ ${v}_{1} < {v}_{2}$
